# Inserting & Editing Items {#sec-editor-common}

Graphs and other objects are added to a page from the ribbon:

- **Analyses** tab: The **Graphs** section groups the graphs into categories (`r keys("Basic")`, `r keys("Business")`, `r keys("Statistical")`, `r keys("SPC")`, `r keys("Survey")`, `r keys("Education")`, `r keys("Social Sciences")`, and `r keys("Sports")`).
  Click a category and select a graph from its menu.
- **Objects** tab: The **Objects** section inserts labels, KPI cards, images, shapes, axes, spacers, and dividers.

Each of these opens an editor dialog.
To edit an existing item, select it and click the `r keys("Edit")` button in the **Objects** section of the **Objects** tab.

An editor dialog has a list of pages along its left side.
The first pages are specific to the item being inserted, and are described in the following chapters.
The remaining pages are shared by most editors and are described below.

## Data Guide {#sec-editor-data-guide}

Graph editors begin with a **Data Guide** page.
This page explains what the graph shows and how its dataset should be laid out.
It includes:

- The variables that the graph uses, which ones are required, and what each one represents.
- A small sample dataset, showing an example of the expected layout.
- How missing data is handled.

## Selecting a Dataset & Variables {#sec-editor-variables}

Most graph editors have the following options on their first page:

**Dataset**: Select the dataset that the graph will use.

**Variables**: Shows the columns that are currently selected for the graph.
Click the `r keys("Select...")` button to open the [**Select Variables**](#sec-select-variables-dlg) dialog and choose them.
Variables marked **(optional)** can be left empty.

\newpage

## General {#sec-editor-graph-general}

The options on this page are shared by all graphs.

**ID**: Enter the graph's ID number.
Each graph in a project should have a unique ID.

### Titles {-}

**Title**: The title shown above the graph.
Click `r keys("Edit...")` to edit its text and formatting.

**Subtitle**: The subtitle shown beneath the title.
Click `r keys("Edit...")` to edit its text and formatting.

**Caption**: The caption shown beneath the graph.
Click `r keys("Edit...")` to edit its text and formatting.

### Background {-}

**Background color**: Select the background color of the plot area.

#### Background Image {-}

**Image**: The image drawn within the plotting area.
Click `r keys("Edit...")` to select the image.

**Opacity**: Sets the transparency of the image.
A value of 0 is fully transparent, whereas 255 is fully opaque.

**Fit**: Select how the image fits inside the plot area:

- **Crop and center**: Crops the image to the plot area, with the center of the image as the origin.
- **Shrink**: Shrinks the image to fit within the plot area, maintaining its aspect ratio.

:::: {.optionssection data-latex=""}
::: {.optionssectiontitle data-latex=""}
Colors
:::

**Color scheme**: Select this option to color the graph's groups from a predefined color scheme.

**Custom color list**: Select this option to enter your own list of colors.

Some graphs (e.g., the **Dueling Pie Chart**) use two sets of colors.
In this case, **Color Scheme 1** and **Color Scheme 2** sections are shown.
::::

:::: {.optionssection data-latex=""}
::: {.optionssectiontitle data-latex=""}
Point Shapes
:::

This section is only shown for graphs that draw points (e.g., the **Line Plot**).

**Shape scheme**: Select this option to draw the groups' points with a predefined set of shapes.

- **Standard Shapes**: A set of common shapes (e.g., circles, squares, and triangles).
- **Semesters**: Shapes representing the fall, spring, and summer semesters (a leaf, a flower, and a sun).

**Custom shape list**: Select this option to enter your own list of shapes.
::::

\newpage

## Annotations & References {#sec-editor-annotations}

The options on this page add notes and reference markers to the graph's plot area.

### Annotations {-}

An annotation is a label drawn on top of the plot, such as a sticky note.
It can optionally have lines drawn from it to points of interest on the plot (e.g., a data point).

When adding or editing an annotation, the following options are available:

**Label**: The annotation's text.
Click `r keys("Edit...")` to edit its text and formatting.

**Anchoring**: Select which part of the label is placed at the anchor point (**Center**, **Top-left corner**, **Top-right corner**, **Bottom-left corner**, or **Bottom-right corner**).

**x-axis**: Enter the anchor point's position along the x axis.

**y-axis**: Enter the anchor point's position along the y axis.

These positions are relative to the plot's axes, not physical positions on the page.

**Interest Points**: Add the points on the plot that lines should be drawn to from the annotation.
Like the anchor point, each point's **x-axis** and **y-axis** positions are relative to the plot's axes.

### Reference Lines {-}

A reference line is drawn across the graph, showing a reference value on its axis (e.g., a goal or a national average).

**Axis**: Select the axis that the reference value is on (**Bottom X**, **Top X**, **Left Y**, or **Right Y**).
The line is drawn across the full length of the opposite axis.

**Position**: Enter the line's position along the axis.

**Label**: Enter the line's label.

**Color**: Select the line's color.

**Label placement**: Select where to show the line's label:

- **Legend**: Shows the label on the graph's legend.
- **Opposite axis**: Shows the label on the opposite axis.

### Reference Areas {-}

A reference area is a shaded range drawn across the graph (e.g., a recession on a time series).

**Axis**: Select the axis that the range is on (**Bottom X**, **Top X**, **Left Y**, or **Right Y**).

**Start**: Enter the start of the range.

**End**: Enter the end of the range.

**Label**: Enter the area's label.

**Color**: Select the area's color.

**Style**: Select how the area is drawn:

- **Solid**: The area is filled solidly and has reference lines on each side.
- **Fade from left to right**: The area is filled with a gradient of the color to transparent, going from left to right (or bottom to top).
  Only the starting side has a reference line.
  This is useful for showing an area with a vague ending point.
- **Fade from right to left**: The area is filled with a gradient of the color to transparent, going from right to left (or top to bottom).
  Only the ending side has a reference line.
  This is useful for showing an area with a vague starting point.

::: {.notesection data-latex=""}
Duplicate reference areas (i.e., ones with the same label and color) are combined into one item on the legend.
This is useful for related events on a plot (e.g., multiple recessions).
:::

\newpage

## Axes {#sec-editor-axes}

The options on this page customize the graph's axes.

**Edit axis**: Select the axis to edit (**Bottom X**, **Top X**, **Left Y**, or **Right Y**).
The remaining options apply to the selected axis.

### Title / Header / Footer {-}

**Title**: The title shown alongside the axis.

**Header**: The label shown at the start of the axis.

**Footer**: The label shown at the end of the axis.

Click `r keys("Edit...")` next to any of these to edit its text and formatting.

### Axis Line {-}

**Color**: Select the color of the axis line.

**Width**: Enter the width of the axis line.

**Style**: Select the axis line's style (**None**, **Solid**, **Dot**, **Long dash**, **Short dash**, or **Dot dash**).

**Cap**: Select what is drawn at the end of the axis line (the right end for horizontal axes, the top for vertical axes):

- **No cap**: Nothing is drawn.
- **Arrow**: An arrow is drawn.

**Reverse**: Check this option to flip the axis.
The range remains the same, but the values and labels are drawn in reverse order along the axis.

### Gridlines {-}

**Color**: Select the color of the gridlines.

**Width**: Enter the width of the gridlines.

**Style**: Select the gridlines' style (**None**, **Solid**, **Dot**, **Long dash**, **Short dash**, or **Dot dash**).

### Tickmarks {-}

**Display**: Select how the tickmarks are drawn:

- **Inner**: The tickmarks are inside the plot.
- **Outer**: The tickmarks are outside the plot.
- **Crossed**: The tickmarks are both inside and outside the plot.
- **No display**: Tickmarks are not shown.

### Labels {-}

**Display**: Select how the axis labels are shown:

- **Custom labels or values**: Shows the custom label (if available) or the numeric value.
- **Only custom labels**: Only shows custom labels.
  Nothing is shown at positions without a custom label.
- **Custom labels and values**: Shows both the numeric value and the custom label.
- **No display**: Labels are not shown.
- **Values**: Only shows the numeric values.

**Number format**: Select how numeric labels are formatted:

- **Value**: Shows the number as-is, with thousands separators.
- **Percentage**: Shows the number as a percentage.
- **Currency**: Shows the number as currency (using your system's settings).
- **Value (simple)**: Shows the number as-is, without thousands separators.

**Orientation**: Select whether the labels are drawn **Parallel** or **Perpendicular** to the axis.

**Perpendicular alignment**: Select how perpendicular labels are aligned:

- **Align with axis line**: The labels are flush against the axis line.
  For example, labels on a left y axis will be flush right (ragged left).
- **Align with boundary**: The labels are aligned against the outer edge of the axis area.
  For example, labels on a left y axis will be flush left (ragged right).
- **Center on axis line**: The labels are centered on the axis line.

**Precision**: Enter the number of decimal places shown for numeric labels.

**Label line length**: Enter the suggested length of each line of a label.
Labels with lines longer than this will be split into multiple lines.

**Double-sided labels**: Check this option to draw the labels on both sides of the axis line.

**Show outer labels**: Check this option to show the first and last labels on the axis (i.e., at the outer edges of the plot).

**Stack labels**: Check this option to stack the labels, where every other label is drawn below the previous one.
This is useful when the labels are long and would otherwise overlap each other.

:::: {.optionssection data-latex=""}
::: {.optionssectiontitle data-latex=""}
Range
:::

**Auto**: Select this option to have the axis range calculated from the data.

**User-defined**: Select this option to enter the range yourself.

For numeric axes, the following options are available:

- **Start**: The first value on the axis.
- **End**: The last value on the axis.
- **Interval**: The distance between each tickmark.
- **Display interval**: How often a label is shown on the tickmarks.
  For example, 2 means that every other tickmark will have a label.

For date axes, the following options are available:

- **Start**: The first date on the axis.
- **End**: The last date on the axis.
- **Interval**: The interval between labels (**Fiscal quarterly**, **Monthly**, **Weekly**, or **Daily**).
::::

### Brackets {-}

Brackets are drawn alongside an axis to group a range of its values under a label (e.g., a fiscal year spanning several months).

When adding or editing a bracket, the following options are available:

- **Label**: The bracket's label.
- **Start**: The start of the bracket's range along the axis.
- **End**: The end of the bracket's range along the axis.
- **Color**: The color of the bracket's lines.
- **Width**: The width of the bracket's lines.
- **Style**: How the bracket is connected to the axis:
  - **Lines**: Regular lines.
  - **Arrow**: An arrow pointing at the axis.
  - **Reverse arrow**: An arrow pointing at the bracket's label.
  - **No connection lines**: Only the bracket itself is drawn.
  - **Curly braces**: The bracket is drawn as a curly brace.

**Add from dataset...**: Click this button to create brackets from a dataset.
Select the **Dataset**, the **Label column** containing the brackets' labels, and the **Value column** containing the positions they span.
The bracket **Style**, **Color**, and **Width** can also be selected here.

Check **Simplify brackets** to shorten repeated date-range labels.
For example, if the brackets contain labels like *1979-80* or *FY1979-1980*, then the first one is kept as-is, but the remaining ones are shortened to *'79-80*.
(This is only applied if all dates are in the same century.)

### Mirroring {-}

**Mirror X axis**: Check this option to show a copy of the bottom x axis on the top of the graph.

**Mirror Y axis**: Check this option to show a copy of the left y axis on the right side of the graph.

\newpage

## Legend {#sec-editor-legend}

The options on this page customize the graph's legend.

**Placement**: Select where the legend is placed relative to the graph (**Right**, **Left**, **Top**, or **Bottom**).
Select **(None)** to not include a legend.

**Include header**: Check this option to show a header on top of the legend.
This is usually the name of the grouping variable.

**Custom title**: Enter a title to use for the legend's header, instead of the default.

**Ring**: For pie-like charts with two rings, select which ring the legend describes (**Outer** or **Inner**).

\newpage

## Placement {#sec-editor-placement}

The options on this page control where the item is placed on the page and how it fits within its cell.

### Grid {-}

A page is laid out as a grid of cells, with one item per cell.

**Rows**: Enter the number of rows in the page's grid.

**Columns**: Enter the number of columns in the page's grid.

**Select the cell where the item will be placed**: Click the cell to place the item in.
Cells that already contain an item show its name; empty cells are labeled *[Empty]*.
If you select a cell that already has an item, then you will be asked whether to replace it.

### Alignment & Scaling {-}

**Horizontal alignment**: Select how the item's content is positioned horizontally within its cell (**Left**, **Centered**, or **Right**).

**Vertical alignment**: Select how the item's content is positioned vertically within its cell (**Top**, **Centered**, or **Bottom**).

::: {.notesection data-latex=""}
The alignment options only apply to tables and labels (including legends).
:::

**Scaling**: Enter the item's scaling, from 0.1 to 10.
This affects the thickness of the item's outline.
For items with a center point (e.g., images and labels), it also affects the size of the item.

**Lock scaling**: Check this option to keep a label's scaling from being adjusted to fit its cell.
Its text will still grow and shrink as the page is zoomed.
This option only affects labels.

### Padding {-}

**Top**, **Right**, **Bottom**, **Left**: Enter the space between the item's content and its outline.
This only affects labels and axes.

### Sizing {-}

**Fit row to content**: Check this option to make the item's row only as tall as the item needs.
By default, rows are stretched equally to fill the page's height.
If two items in the same row have this checked, then the row will be the height of the taller item.

**Fixed width**: Check this option to give the item only the width it needs within its row.
By default, items in a row are stretched equally to fill the page's width.
This is usually used for legends placed next to a graph.

### Outline {-}

**Color**: Select the color of the item's outline.

**Width**: Enter the width of the outline.

**Style**: Select the outline's style (**Solid**, **Dot**, **Long dash**, **Short dash**, or **Dot dash**).

**Top**, **Right**, **Bottom**, **Left**: Check which sides of the item have an outline.

### Canvas Margins {-}

**Top**, **Right**, **Bottom**, **Left**: Enter the margins around the item within its cell.
These only take effect when the item is the only one in its cell.

\newpage

## Accessibility {#sec-editor-accessibility}

The options on this page control the accessibility attributes written for the item when it is exported to SVG (or an HTML dashboard).
These attributes describe the item to screen readers.

**Automatically manage accessibility**: Check this option to have the program generate the item's accessibility attributes.
For graphs, this includes a description of the graph's data and presentation.

### Manual Settings {-}

These options are only available when **Automatically manage accessibility** is unchecked.

**ARIA Label**: Enter the text that screen readers will read for the item.

**Role**: Select the item's role:

- **(default)**: Uses the default role for the item.
- **figure**: The item is a figure (e.g., a graph with its title and caption).
- **img**: The item is an image.
- **presentation**: The item is decorative and has no meaning to convey.

**ARIA Hidden**: Check this option to hide the item from screen readers.
This is useful for purely decorative items.
